cause_quote: The diff added `return !hasActiveAgentDatabaseLease(params.agentId, params.env);` and `await withAgentDatabaseMaintenanceLease({ env }, async () => {`, so an idle agent could trigger a global maintenance request for cursor bookkeeping while another agent held a writer lease.
user_saw: `openclaw doctor --non-interactive` could exit with a database-in-use error on healthy transcript history when one configured agent was idle and another held a writer lease.
summary: Doctor now checks for active writers across all agents and defers migration cursor bookkeeping while any writer is active, while still requiring exclusive maintenance for actual repairs.
reasoning: The parent already ran the historical transcript migration and could record completion on the idle agent's database while another agent held a lease. PR #133563 paired a per-agent preflight with an existing global maintenance guard, creating the false refusal, and I checked that the later PostgreSQL rewrite preserved the same predicate for native databases.
